arxiv-2012-13454.title: Why Neural Machine Translation Prefers Empty Outputs
arxiv-2012-13454.creator: Xing Shi, Yijun Xiao, Kevin Knight
arxiv-2012-13454.description: Abstract We investigate why neural machine translation (NMT) systems assign high probability to empty translations. We find two explanations. First, label smoothing makes correct-length translations less confident, making it easier for the empty translation to outscore them. Second, NMT systems use the same, high-frequency EoS word type to end all target sentences, regardless of length.

arxiv-2105-04341.title: Quantum networks based on color centers in diamond
arxiv-2105-04341.creator: Maximilian Ruf, Noel H. Wan, Hyeongrak Choi, Dirk Englund, Ronald Hanson
arxiv-2105-04341.description: Abstract With the ability to transfer and process quantum information, large-scale quantum networks will enable a suite of fundamentally new applications, from quantum communications to distributed sensing, metrology, and computing. This perspective reviews requirements for quantum network nodes and color centers in diamond as suitable node candidates.

arxiv-2105-09067.title: Localization and Tracking of User-Defined Points on Deformable Objects for Robotic Manipulation This work was partially supported by the German Federal Ministry of Education and Research (BMBF) under the grant no. 16SV8406.
arxiv-2105-09067.creator: Sven Dittus, Benjamin Alt, Andreas Hermann, Darko Katic and Rainer Jäkel, Jürgen Fleischer
arxiv-2105-09067.description: Abstract This paper introduces an efficient procedure to localize user-defined points on the surface of deformable objects and track their positions in 3D space over time. To cope with a deformable object’s infinite number of DOF, we propose a discretized deformation field, which is estimated during runtime using a multi-step non-linear solver pipeline.

arxiv-2106-03783.title: An Information-theoretic Approach to Distribution Shifts
arxiv-2106-03783.creator: Marco Federici, Ryota Tomioka, Patrick Forré
arxiv-2106-03783.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Marco Federici, Ryota Tomioka, Patrick Forré. Safely deploying machine learning models to the real world is often a challenging process. Models trained with data obtained from a specific geographic location tend to fail when queried with data obtained elsewhere, agents trained in a simulation can struggle to adapt when deployed in the real world or novel environments, and neural networks that are fit to a subset of the population might carry some selection bias into their decision process.

arxiv-2110-11226.title: Accelerating Genetic Programming using GPUs
arxiv-2110-11226.creator: Vimarsh Sathia 1 , Venkataramana Ganesh 2 , Shankara Rao Thejaswi Nanditale 2, cs17b046@cse.iitm.ac.in, gvenkatarama@nvidia.com, snanditale@nvidia.com
arxiv-2110-11226.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Vimarsh Sathia 1 , Venkataramana Ganesh 2 , Shankara Rao Thejaswi Nanditale 2, cs17b046@cse.iitm.ac.in, gvenkatarama@nvidia.com, snanditale@nvidia.com. Genetic Programming (GP), an evolutionary learning technique, has multiple applications in machine learning such as curve fitting, data modelling, feature selection, classification etc. GP has several inherent parallel steps, making it an ideal candidate for GPU based parallelization. This paper describes a GPU accelerated stack-based variant of the generational GP algorithm which can be used for symbolic regression and binary classification.

arxiv-2111-01389.title: Physics of star formation history and the luminosity function of galaxies therefrom
arxiv-2111-01389.creator: Masataka Fukugita, Masahiro Kawasaki
arxiv-2111-01389.description: Abstract We show that the star formation history, the reionization history and the present luminosity function of galaxies are reproduced in a simple gravitational collapse model within the Λ \Lambda CDM regime to almost a quantitative accuracy, when the physical conditions, the Jeans criterion and the cooling process, are taken into account.

arxiv-2209-03251.title: Explicit Low-Bandwidth Evaluation Schemes for Weighted Sums of Reed-Solomon-Coded Symbols
arxiv-2209-03251.creator: Han Mao Kiah, Wilton Kim, Stanislav Kruglik, San Ling, Huaxiong Wang School of Physical and Mathematical Sciences, Nanyang Technological University, Singapore email: {hmkiah, wilt0002, stanislav.kruglik, lingsan, hxwang}@ntu.edu.sg
arxiv-2209-03251.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Han Mao Kiah, Wilton Kim, Stanislav Kruglik, San Ling, Huaxiong Wang School of Physical and Mathematical Sciences, Nanyang Technological University, Singapore email: {hmkiah, wilt0002, stanislav.kruglik, lingsan, hxwang}@ntu.edu.sg. Motivated by applications in distributed storage, distributed computing, and homomorphic secret sharing, we study communication-efficient schemes for computing linear combinations of coded symbols.

arxiv-2211-09113.title: On Measuring the Intrinsic Few-Shot Hardness of Datasets
arxiv-2211-09113.creator: Xinran Zhao, Shikhar MurtyChristopher D. Manning Computer Science Department, Stanford University {xzhaoar,smurty,manning}@cs.stanford.edu
arxiv-2211-09113.description: Abstract While advances in pre-training have led to dramatic improvements in few-shot learning of NLP tasks, there is limited understanding of what drives successful few-shot adaptation in datasets. In particular, given a new dataset and a pre-trained model, what properties of the dataset make it few-shot learnable and are these properties independent of the specific adaptation techniques used?

arxiv-2211-16126.title: Joint Neural Architecture and Hyperparameter Search for Correlated Time Series Forecasting DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX Conference: the 2023 International Conference on Management of Data, June 18–23, 2023, Seattle, WA, USA.; 15.00 Price: ; ISBN: 978-1-4503-XXXX-X/18/06 Thanks: *corresponding authors: D. Zh
arxiv-2211-16126.creator: Xinle Wu, Dalin Zhang ∗ , Miao Zhang, Chenjuan Guo, Bin Yang ∗ , Christian S. Jensen Department of Computer Science, Aalborg University, Denmark
arxiv-2211-16126.description: Abstract . Sensors in cyber-physical systems often capture interconnected processes and thus emit correlated time series (CTS), the forecasting of which enables important applications. The key to successful CTS forecasting is to uncover the temporal dynamics of time series and the spatial correlations among time series. Deep learning-based solutions exhibit impressive performance at discerning these aspects.

arxiv-2304-14563.title: Causality and stability in first-order conformal anisotropic hydrodynamics
arxiv-2304-14563.creator: Fábio S. Bemfica, Mauricio Martinez, Masoud Shokri
arxiv-2304-14563.description: Abstract We formulate the first-order dissipative anisotropic hydrodynamical theory for a relativistic conformal uncharged fluid, which generalizes the Bemfica-Disconzi-Noronha-Kovtun first-order viscous fluid framework. Our approach maintains causal behavior in the nonlinear regime with or without general relativity coupling, and we derive and analyze the constraints on transport coefficients imposed by causality.

arxiv-2409-19492.title: MedHalu : Hallucinations in Responses to Healthcare Queries by Large Language Models
arxiv-2409-19492.creator: Vibhor Agarwal, Yiqiao Jin, Mohit Chandra, Munmun De Choudhury, Srijan Kumar, Nishanth Sastry
arxiv-2409-19492.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are starting to complement traditional information seeking mechanisms such as web search. LLM-powered chatbots like ChatGPT are gaining prominence among the general public. AI chatbots are also increasingly producing content on social media platforms. However, LLMs are also prone to hallucinations, generating plausible yet factually incorrect or fabricated information.

arxiv-2411-15536.title: Four-Qubit CHSH Games
arxiv-2411-15536.creator: Joaquim Jusseau, Hamza Jaffali, Frédéric Holweck
arxiv-2411-15536.description: Abstract . In this paper, the CHSH quantum game is extended to four players. This is achieved by exploring all possible 4-variable Boolean functions to identify those that yield a game scenario with a quantum advantage using a specific entangled state. Notably, two new four-player quantum games are presented.

arxiv-2505-03292.title: Understanding Decoherence of the Boron Vacancy Center in Hexagonal Boron Nitride
arxiv-2505-03292.description: Abstract Hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) has emerged as a significant material for quantum sensing, particularly due to its ability to host spin active defects, such as the negatively charged boron vacancy (V − B {}_{\mathrm{B}}^{-} center). The optical addressability of the V − B {}_{\mathrm{B}}^{-} center and hBN’s 2D structure enable high spatial resolution and integration into various platforms.

arxiv-2506-03736.title: Influence of photon inverse emission on forward–backward asymmetry in dilepton production at LHC
arxiv-2506-03736.creator: V. A. Zykunov
arxiv-2506-03736.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by V. A. Zykunov. Contribution of photon inverse emission to the dilepton production process in hadron collisions for Large Hadron Collider (LHC) experimental program is calculated in details. Numerical analysis of inverse emission effects on observable quantities (cross sections and forward-backward asymmetry) is performed in a wide kinematical region including the CMS LHC experiment in Run3/HL regime which corresponds to ultra-high energies and dilepton invariant masses.

arxiv-2508-06250.title: Dirty Bits in Low-Earth Orbit: The Carbon Footprint of Launching Computers DOI: 10.1145/3757892.3757896 Conference: ACM SIGENERGY Energy Informatics Review; Volume 5 Issue 2; July 2025 ACM SIGENERGY Energy Informatics Review
arxiv-2508-06250.creator: Robin Ohs, Gregory F. Stock, Andreas Schmidt, Juan A. Fraire, Holger Hermanns
arxiv-2508-06250.description: Abstract . Low-Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites are increasingly proposed for communication and in-orbit computing, achieving low-latency global services. However, their sustainability remains largely unexamined. This paper investigates the carbon footprint of computing in space, focusing on lifecycle emissions from launch over orbital operation to re-entry.

pmc-10617062.title: Depression and anxiety symptoms among Vietnamese migrants in Japan during the COVID-19 pandemic
pmc-10617062.creator: Tadashi Yamashita, Pham Nguyen Quy, Emi Nogami, Erina Seto-Suh, Chika Yamada, Saori Iwamoto, Kyoko Shimazawa, Kenji Kato
pmc-10617062.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). This study aimed to examine the mental health status and related factors among Vietnamese migrants in Japan during the COVID-19 pandemic. We conducted an online cross-sectional survey between September 21 and October 21, 2021. Along with Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) and Generalized Anxiety Disorder 7-item (GAD-7) scores, we collected data on demographics, changes in socioeconomic status due to the pandemic, language proficiency, social support, and health conditions. Multivariate logistic regression was performed to identify factors related to symptoms of depression and anxiety.

pmc-10804068.title: Molecular Identification of Juglans Regia Endophyte LTL-G3, Its Antifungal Potential and Bioactive Substances
pmc-10804068.creator: Yuanru Hao, Jianchao Hui, Tianyu Du, Xiangrui Ge, Meizhi Zhai
pmc-10804068.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Background: Endophyte is one of the potential biocontrol agents for inhibiting plant pathogens. However, the mechanisms and characteristics involved in the inhibition of different phytopathogenic fungi by endophytes, especially walnut endophytes, are still largely unknown.Objectives: The present study aimed to identify the walnut endophytic fungus LTL-G3 from a genetic point of view, assess the strain’s antifungal activity, and determine the bioactivities of the substances it produces against plant pathogens.Materials and Methods: The homologous sequence of strain LTL-G3 was examined, and typical strains

pmc-11367975.title: Diagnostic value of miR-34a in Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia in children and its correlation with rehabilitation effect
pmc-11367975.creator: Min Li, Leijuan Lu, Hong Xu
pmc-11367975.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundMycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia (MPP) is responsible for 20 to 40% of all cases of pneumonia acquired by children and shows an increasing incidence year by year. The aim of this study was to investigate the expression of miR-34a in children with MPP and its diagnostic value, and further explore the relationship between miR-34a and the rehabilitation effect of children with MPP.MethodsThe expression level of miR-34a was detected by RT-qPCR, and the clinical value of miR-34a was analyzed by ROC analysis.

pmc-11509119.title: The Effect of Spinosad on the Oak Lace Bug Corythucha arcuata (Hemiptera: Tingidae)—A Preliminary Study Performed Under Laboratory Conditions
pmc-11509119.creator: Ciprian George Fora, Artúr Botond Csorba, Adalbert Balog, Muhammad Haseeb, Lambert HB Kanga
pmc-11509119.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Simple SummaryThe oak lace bug is a rapidly spreading oak forest pest in Europe. These days, chemical control has been largely reduced in favor of biological methods due to the high biodiversity values of these forests.

pmc-11610071.title: Developing a model for clinical teaching with emotional intelligence
pmc-11610071.creator: Athar Omid, Fariba Haghani, Nahid Toufan
pmc-11610071.description: BackgroundClinical teaching is an essential part of medical education and clinical teacher must acquire the necessary competencies to perform such a role. In this regard, there is emphasis on emotional intelligence as an essential competency. The aim of this study was to develop a model for clinical teaching with emotional intelligence based on the experiences of clinical teachers.

pmc-12541093.title: Understanding individual neurodegenerative progression in Parkinson’s disease through normative modelling
pmc-12541093.creator: Charlotte Fraza, Barbora Rehák Bučková, Martin E Johansson, Rick C Helmich, Andre F Marquand, Christian F Beckmann
pmc-12541093.description: Parkinson’s disease (PD) is a neurodegenerative disorder with motor symptoms (e.g., bradykinesia, tremors) and non-motor symptoms (e.g., cognitive deficits). Symptom progression varies across individuals, possibly due to differences in the spread of disease pathology. This study investigates individual-level gray matter atrophy in PD patients compared to a reference cohort, modeling neurobiological trajectories to understand symptom progression.

pmc-12564931.title: Low-Dose Indapamide vs. Hydrochlorothiazide in Idiopathic Hypercalciuria: A Randomized Prospective Trial
pmc-12564931.creator: Maria Peraire, Jorge Guimerà, Antonia Costa-Bauzá, Pilar Sanchís, Felix Grases, Enrique Pieras, Shih-Hua Lin
pmc-12564931.description: Background: Idiopathic hypercalciuria (IH) is the most common genetic metabolic disorder in patients with urinary stones and is usually treated with thiazide-type diuretics. However, direct evidence comparing low-dose indapamide and hydrochlorothiazide is scarce. This study aimed to compare their safety, efficacy and adherence in patients with IH.

pmc-12584832.title: Sestrins: a new therapeutic target for endothelial dysfunction and cardiovascular disease prevention
pmc-12584832.creator: Cheng Li, Xu Zhang
pmc-12584832.description: BackgroundSestrins are a highly conserved family of proteins that have garnered significant attention for their critical roles in regulating cellular stress responses, antioxidative defense, energy metabolism, and cell survival. Endothelial dysfunction, a pivotal early event in the development of cardiovascular diseases (CVDs), is strongly associated with oxidative stress, inflammation, and disruption of vascular homeostasis.

pmc-12698317.title: Individual Malaria Case and Case Cluster Status in the Capital Region of the Republic of Korea, 2024
pmc-12698317.creator: Mijeong Ko, YUN JEONG SEO, Hyunmi Kim, Kyungwon Hwang, 미정 고, 윤정 서, 현미 김, 경원 황
pmc-12698317.description: ObjectivesWe analyzed malaria cases and cluster outbreaks in the capital city between 2022 and 2024 to provide baseline data to guide effective prevention and response strategies.MethodsAll malaria cases reported in the Integrated Disease Control Information System between January 1, 2022, and December 31, 2024, were included. Annual trends, demographics, regional distributions, and case clusters were analyzed.

pmc-12823674.title: A denoising method for aeroengine gas path electrostatic signal of low signal-to-noise ratio based on IMFs optimized reconstruction and wavelet threshold
pmc-12823674.creator: Chaoying Yan, Yan Liu, Feng Lu
pmc-12823674.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Electrostatic monitoring technology for aero-engines has demonstrated considerable capability in early fault warning. However, raw electrostatic signals often contain significant noise and exhibit low signal-to-noise ratios, making denoising essential to improve the accuracy of fault-related information extraction. To address the issue of coupled noise in electrostatic signals, this study introduces methodologies based on Improved Complete Ensemble EMD with Adaptive Noise (ICEEMDAN), Autocorrelation Function (ACF), and Wavelet Soft-thresholding (WTD).

pmc-12896296.title: A mixed-method study on the screening practices and barriers to diabetic microvascular complications by general practitioners in community health centers of Xiamen, China
pmc-12896296.creator: Zhang-Yan Chen, Cui-Ling Huang, Cheng-Dian Lan, Hua Yang
pmc-12896296.description: BackgroundEarly screening and management of diabetic microvascular complications are of crucial importance for preventing diabetes progression and improving patient outcomes. This study aimed to assess the current status of screening practices employed by general practitioners (GPs) in community health centers (CHCs) in Xiamen, China, and identify implementation barriers.

pmc-13215386.title: Genetic trends in body measurements at birth for Arabian horse in Türkiye
pmc-13215386.creator: Özlem Hacan, Mustafa Tekerli, Samet Çinkaya, Mustafa Demirtaş
pmc-13215386.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Changes in genetic variation in body measurements are a subject of interest. This study aimed to understand the changes in the genetic effects of body measurement at birth in Turkish Arabian foals over the years. Furthermore, estimating the sources of variation in body measurements at birth in Turkish Arabian foals, considering additive genetic, maternal genetic, and maternal permanent effects and the covariance between offspring and dams in animal models, was the objective of this study.

pmc-13323696.title: Tibial transverse transport promotes diabetic foot ulcer healing by regulating miR-182-5p
pmc-13323696.creator: Tongliang Xie, Haojie Li, Zuyan Sun, Rui Li, Wenliang Huang
pmc-13323696.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs) represent a major complication of diabetes, characterized by impaired wound healing. Tibial transverse transport (TTT), a mechanical intervention technique, has shown clinical efficacy in promoting DFU repair; however, its molecular mechanisms remain largely unclear. This study aimed to explore the role of microRNAs (miRNAs) in the TTT-mediated healing of DFUs and to elucidate their regulatory effects on fibroblast function under hyperglycemic conditions. A diabetic rabbit model with full-thickness foot ulcers was established and treated with TTT.

pmc-13382262.title: The Qur'anic heart and converging evidence from contemporary cardiac science: From qalb to cardioception
pmc-13382262.creator: Ahmed S. BaHammam
pmc-13382262.description: For most of recorded history, the heart was considered far more than a pump. The Qur'an and Sunnah (ahadith) describe it as the seat of reasoning, faith, emotion, and moral accountability, employing a vocabulary of at least four distinct cardiac terms (qalb, fu'ad, lubb, and sadr) that appear over 200 times in contexts extending well beyond circulation.

pmc-13404913.title: Computational mapping of productive POI–E3 ligase conformations to guide de novo degrader design: application to WEE1 and PKMYT1 PROTACs
pmc-13404913.creator: Husam Nassar, Matthias Schmidt, Hany S Ibrahim, Dina Robaa, Wolfgang Sippl

pmc-13553811.title: Perfectionism and anxiety sensitivity in soccer referees: the mediating role of distress tolerance
pmc-13553811.creator: J. J. Martínez-Oller, A. P. Pacheco-Unguetti, J. González-Hernández
pmc-13553811.description: BackgroundThe present research aimed to analyze the relationship between perfectionism, sensitivity to anxiety, and distress tolerance in soccer referees.MethodsThe sample consisted of 268 Spanish soccer referees from different categories and experience levels, and a correlational and cross-sectional design was used.

pmc-13574786.title: Impact of Chamaecrista rotundifolia cover cropping on soil elemental cycling in karst agroecosystems
pmc-13574786.creator: Zhengfu Yue, Shoushan Sheng, Liang Peng, Wei Xu, Jing Zhang, Dongming Wu, Beibei Liu, Qinfen Li, Rongshu Dong, Hanting Cheng, Yukun Zou
pmc-13574786.description: Karst desertification causes severe soil erosion, hydrological imbalance, and biodiversity loss, thereby threatening ecosystem resilience and agricultural productivity. Soil carbon (C), nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), and sulfur (S) cycling underpin ecosystem stability, yet how agricultural management practices regulate multi-element cycling in degraded karst agroecosystems remains poorly understood.

pmc-13590920.title: Longitudinal 3D quantification of joint space from CT images: Semi-automatic segmentation and feasibility of nnU-Net automation
pmc-13590920.creator: Jean Baptiste Deloges, Stéphanie Uk, Jordan Cohen, Marianne Bourguignon, Jean Denis Laredo, Klaus Engelke, Christine Chappard
pmc-13590920.description: ObjectivesThe most commonly imaging techniques used in knee osteoarthritis (OA) of the are Xrays and MRI. Computed tomography (CT) however, has his own advantages, especially three-dimensional high-resolution representation of subchondral bone and epiphyseal bone structure. Addition of a method allowing 3D joint space (JS) quantification would improve the clinical value of CT in knee OA follow-up.
